summary: Sidecar proxy in Private VPC causing duplicate rate accounting and intermittent 429s (healthcheck + auth-rewrite)
description:
Issue summary:
BrightFleet reports intermittent 429 responses from Redwood endpoints after migrating to Private VPC (on-prem control plane + sidecar proxy). The errors spike during orchestration windows and coincide with their local health checks and an upstream auth token rewrite performed by the sidecar.

Impact:
- Several production ingestion jobs and a small set of interactive chat sessions hit 429s for short windows (~30-90s) several times per hour.
- Customer sees increased tail latency and job retries; business impact is degraded SLA for their logistics dashboard.

Environment:
- Deployment: Private (customer-managed control plane) in BrightFleet's eu-west cluster
- Sidecar proxy: custom envoy-based sidecar operated by customer, v1.14 (with Authorization header rewrite)
- Redwood components: private API gateway + local rate-limiter (per-tenant and per-route accounting enabled)
- Health checks: /hc polled every 10s by k8s readiness probe and by a local monitoring agent

Timeline / observed pattern:
- 2026-03-09 09:18 UTC: First reports of 429s after a config change on customer side (sidecar upgrade).
- Spikes are short-lived and reproducible during coordination events: deploys, cron ingest windows, and during periodic monitoring checks.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Deploy the sidecar with Authorization header rewrite enabled (token translation from x-internal-token to standard Bearer).
2. Start an ingest job that makes concurrent multi-route requests (50 concurrent short requests).
3. Ensure k8s readiness probe and local monitoring agent poll /hc every 10s.
4. Observe 429s on a subset of requests and increased rate-limit counters in the local rate-limiter telemetry.

Observed behavior:
- Rate-limiter telemetry shows double-counting of many requests: each logical request appears twice in accounting for a short window (~200ms - 2s).
- 429s appear to correlate with bursts of healthcheck or monitoring probe traffic immediately preceding the spike.
- Some requests show a modified path (route normalization) in logs after sidecar rewrite which aligns with the second accounting entry.

Expected behavior:
- Health probes and token-translation proxying should not cause duplicated accounting or erroneous per-route token increments.
- 429s should only be returned when tenant or route quota legitimately exhausted.

Logs & traces (excerpt included below) and customer-provided artifacts are attached in support bundle (request-id: bf-20260309-0918).

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Guidance on how to configure sidecar/monitoring to avoid contributing to tenant quota
- Request for temporary quota bump while we investigate (customer provided business justification)

comments: 2026-03-09 - Ava Martinez (Support): Initial triage and asked customer for pcap and sidecar config. Recommended reducing probe frequency as stop-gap.
2026-03-09 - BrightFleet (Customer): Uploaded sidecar config and support bundle. Confirmed they perform header rewrite for backward compatibility with their auth system.

2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel (SRE): We reproduced locally with envoy sidecar config. Suspect accounting duplicate when sidecar re-emits request to internal API after rewrite — double-count observed in rate-limiter metrics.
2026-03-11 - BrightFleet: Applied a stop-gap change to exclude /hc from external monitoring agent. Observed reduction in 429 frequency but not eliminated.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Created internal INT ticket for a de-dup key + healthcheck-exemption patch. Requested temporary quota bump (approved) and provided config guidance to customer.
investigation_notes: Reproduction was successful in lab using customer sidecar config (envoy v1.14). When the sidecar rewrites auth header it performs an internal re-emit to the API gateway, which is being counted as a separate request by the rate-limiter before the original request's accounting completes.

Root cause hypothesis: sidecar's re-emit lacks a unique request ID header expected by the rate-limiter de-dup logic. Gateway sees two requests with different attributes (original and rewritten) and increments per-route counters twice.

Healthcheck and monitoring probes amplify the issue because they trigger rapid, short-lived requests that race with the re-emit path and fall inside the same accounting window, making double-counting more likely.

Telemetry: correlation between 'x-request-id' presence and single-count behavior. Requests that include x-request-id are only counted once. Sidecar does not preserve x-request-id consistently post-rewrite.
Scope: affects private deployments where a customer-managed sidecar rewrites auth and re-issues requests. Hosted customers not impacted.
Related internal follow-ups: INT-4412 created to add de-dup acceptance on request-id and to expose a config flag for healthcheck exemption in private control plane rate-limiter.
Customer logs also show occasional 5xx during the same windows; we believe those are downstream errors retried by the sidecar and then counted separately by rate-limiter.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigations applied: customer excluded /hc from their external monitoring agent polling and lowered readiness probe frequency to 30s. Temporary tenant quota bump granted for 48 hours to ease immediate impact.

Medium-term: INT-4412 will add a de-dup check based on x-request-id and a configurable header (X-Redwood-Skip-Accounting) that private deploys can enable for health-checks and trusted sidecar re-emits.

Customer was given a recommended sidecar config snippet to preserve x-request-id across rewrites and to avoid re-emitting the full request when possible. Also recommended to tag internal probes with X-Redwood-Skip-Accounting until the platform patch lands.
Patch timeline: PR created and under review (github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/892). Targeted rollout to private control plane images in two weeks after validation and canary.
recommended_actions: Customer: Apply sidecar change to preserve x-request-id header across rewrites and re-emits.
Customer: Mark monitoring probes with X-Redwood-Skip-Accounting or exclude /hc from tenant-level counting until patch is live.
Support/SRE: Merge de-dup PR and add feature flag to private control plane to ignore marked probes.
Support: Monitor tenant rate-limiter metrics closely during next customer deploy and remove temporary quota bump after stabilization.
